„Optimizacija za uštedu električne energije često znači veću potrošnju vode na lokaciji, i obrnuto. Pravi izazov modernog AI računalstva nije samo smanjenje jednog izoliranog faktora, već postizanje termodinamičke ravnoteže prilagođene lokalnom energetskom i hidrološkom ekosustavu.“

Predstavljanje podatkovnih centara kao primarnih krivaca za lokalne nestašice vode često služi za senzacionalističke medijske naslove i izazivanje javnog otpora (NIMBY - Not In My Back Yard efekt). Iako je iznimno važno inzistirati na odgovornom upravljanju resursima, važno je uočiti razlike:

  • Podatkovni centri posluju pod rigoroznim financijskim i ekološkim (ESG) kontrolama gdje voda predstavlja direktan trošak, zbog čega IT industrija neprekidno ulaže u optimizaciju ciklusa hlađenja.
  • Sve veći broj novih objekata koristi tehničku (sivu) vodu, pročišćene komunalne otpadne vode ili kišnicu, umjesto da crpi pitku vodu iz javnog vodovoda.
  • Masovnim usvajanjem tehnologija poput Direct-to-Chip (DLC) i uronjenog hlađenja, lokalna potrošnja vode na novim objektima u potpunosti teži prema nuli.

Pitanje "Koliko vode zapravo troše podatkovni centri?" nema jednostavan dvoznamenkasti odgovor. Vodeni otisak računalne infrastrukture direktna je posljedica fizikalnih izbora u termodinamičkom dizajnu, geografskoj lokaciji i energetskom miksu mreže. Iako apsolutne brojke od milijun litara vode dnevno zvuče zabrinjavajuće, usporedba s komunalnim gubicima, golf terenima i poljoprivredom jasno pokazuje da podatkovni centri nisu primarni uzročnik globalne vodne krize. Pod pritiskom regulative i cijena resursa, IT industrija je danas jedan od najbržih pokretača tehnoloških inovacija u upravljanju vodom.
content_en:
Every time we send a query to an artificial intelligence model, start streaming high-definition video, or store a file, we unconsciously activate a complex physical system in the background. The term "cloud" has created an illusion of immateriality—a vision where data travels weightlessly through the air, detached from physical constraints. However, the reality of computing remains deeply rooted in the laws of thermodynamics, steel, and silicon.

At the center of this infrastructure are data centers, facilities designed to convert electrical power into computations (compute). Yet, according to the first law of thermodynamics, virtually all electrical energy consumed by microprocessors is ultimately converted into heat. The more we compute, the more heat we generate. You can observe a similar phenomenon in the heating of personal computers.

Initially, standard power density per server rack ranged between $5\text{ kW}$ and $10\text{ kW}$. Air cooling, directing cold air through isolated aisles, was entirely sufficient to maintain hardware components at stable operating temperatures. However, the advent of generative artificial intelligence and modern AI accelerator chips disrupted this model. Today's AI clusters require power densities of $40\text{ kW}$, $80\text{ kW}$, and even upwards of $100\text{ kW}$ per individual rack.

At these levels of heat flux, air simply ceases to function as an effective thermal transfer medium. The specific heat capacity of air is:

$$c_p \approx 1.005\text{ kJ/(kg}\cdot\text{K)}$$

By contrast, water has a substantially higher specific heat capacity:

$$c_p \approx 4.184\text{ kJ/(kg}\cdot\text{K)}$$

Due to this fundamental physical property, combined with the significantly higher density of liquids compared to gases, water is thousands of times more effective as a heat dissipation medium per unit volume. To prevent thermal degradation of processors whose operating temperatures must not exceed $85^\circ\text{C}$, the industry has shifted toward the widespread adoption of liquid cooling.

When we discuss the "digital transformation," we are fundamentally discussing the reallocation of physical resources. This brings us to the core question: How much water do data centers actually consume?

Two Dimensions of Consumption

To accurately measure a data center's impact on freshwater resources, it is essential to evaluate the entire energy lifecycle. The water footprint of computing infrastructure is split into two primary components: direct (on-site) and indirect (off-site / utility) consumption.

TOTAL WATER FOOTPRINT (Scope 1 + Scope 2)
DIRECT CONSUMPTION On-site at data center facility
Scope 1
  • Cooling Towers
  • Evaporative Cooling
  • On-site Processes
INDIRECT CONSUMPTION At upstream power generation plants
Scope 2
  • Thermal Power Plants
  • Nuclear Power Plants
  • Hydroelectric Reservoirs

Direct Water Footprint

This is the most visible form of consumption. It represents water physically transported to or drawn on-site at the data center facility and utilized within cooling systems. As heat rejection systems expel thermal loads from server halls, water is atomized in cooling towers or evaporative coolers. A portion of this water evaporates into the atmosphere to cool the remaining liquid, leveraging the high latent heat of vaporization of water.

Indirect Water Footprint

This portion of the footprint often remains invisible because it occurs not at the server site, but at upstream utility power generation plants. Every kilowatt-hour ($1\text{ kWh}$) drawn by a data center from the electrical grid carries its own embedded water footprint:

  • Thermal and Nuclear Power Plants: Utilize massive volumes of cooling water in condensers to condense steam driving turbines.
  • Hydroelectric Facilities: While consuming no fossil fuels, reservoir dams feature expansive open surface areas experiencing continuous water evaporation (reservoir surface evaporation losses).

If a data center draws power from an electrical grid dominated by coal or nuclear energy, its indirect water footprint can easily exceed the volume of water physically consumed on-site by several multiples.

Distinction: Water Withdrawal vs. Water Consumption

In sustainability analysis, it is critical to distinguish between two terms frequently conflated in public discourse:

  1. Water Withdrawal: The total volume of water diverted from a natural source (rivers, lakes, aquifers) or municipal utility network. After cycling through cooling loops in closed or semi-open circuits without evaporation, the vast majority is returned directly to the source watershed (often only with a slight thermal elevation).
  2. Water Consumption: The volume of water permanently removed from the local watershed during cooling via phase change into vapor (evaporation) or integration into waste sludge.

When assessing environmental stress on local communities and drought-prone regions, water consumption is the paramount metric, as atmospheric water vapor does not guarantee precipitation return to the same local basin.

Standard Industry Metrics: WUE and the Thermodynamic Trade-off of PUE vs. WUE

To establish standardized water accounting, The Green Grid consortium introduced the WUE (Water Usage Effectiveness) metric in 2011. Just as PUE evaluates facility energy efficiency, WUE quantifies the liters of water consumed per kilowatt-hour of electricity delivered to IT equipment (servers, networking hardware, and storage arrays).

The foundational formula for on-site water consumption is:

$$WUE_{\text{site}} = \frac{\text{Annual On-Site Water Consumption (L)}}{\text{Annual IT Equipment Energy Consumption (kWh)}}$$

When assessing total environmental impact, including upstream water consumed in grid electricity generation, the expanded metric is applied:

$$WUE_{\text{source}} = WUE_{\text{site}} + WUE_{\text{utility}}$$

where $WUE_{\text{utility}}$ represents the specific water consumption rate of power plants per unit of generated electricity across the regional energy grid mix.

WUE values vary substantially depending on thermodynamic architecture and local climate conditions:

  • Traditional Evaporative Systems (Open Cooling Towers): $1.5 - 2.5\text{ L/kWh}$ (frequently exceeding $3.0\text{ L/kWh}$ in hot, arid zones).
  • Hybrid Systems with Economizer Cycles: $0.5 - 1.2\text{ L/kWh}$.
  • Closed-Loop Air-Cooled Systems (Dry Coolers / DX Compressors): $0.0 - 0.2\text{ L/kWh}$ on-site, albeit at a notable electrical energy penalty.
  • Modern Hyperscaler Targets: Achieving operational $WUE_{\text{site}} \le 0.3\text{ L/kWh}$, primarily by eliminating evaporative phases during cooler months.

The Thermodynamic Paradox: PUE vs. WUE

Over the past two decades, data center engineering focused intensely on minimizing Power Usage Effectiveness (PUE):

$$PUE = \frac{\text{Total Facility Power}}{\text{IT Equipment Power}} \rightarrow 1.0$$

The simplest and thermodynamically most efficient method to push PUE below $1.15$ was widespread adoption of evaporative cooling.

The underlying physics lies in the exceptionally high latent heat of vaporization of water ($h_{fg} \approx 2260\text{ kJ/kg}$ at atmospheric pressure). Evaporating a single liter of water absorbs as much thermal energy as heating the same mass of water from $0^\circ\text{C}$ to $100^\circ\text{C}$ more than five times over. Harnessing this phase change eliminates the continuous operation of power-hungry mechanical refrigeration chillers.

This creates a pronounced engineering trade-off:

  • Optimizing for PUE (Energy Conservation): Cooling towers and adiabatic economizers are deployed. Compressors remain idle, cooling electrical power drops to a minimum, and PUE reaches near-ideal values. However, the trade-off is massive local water consumption, with hundreds of thousands of cubic meters of water permanently evaporating into the atmosphere.
  • Optimizing for WUE (Water Conservation): Evaporation is switched off, transitioning the facility to closed-loop dry coolers or direct mechanical chillers. On-site water consumption drops to zero, but electrical power consumption for fans and compressors surges, degrading PUE. If that supplemental electrical energy is supplied by thermal power plants with once-through cooling, the water burden simply shifts from the server facility to upstream power stations.

Cooling architecture decisions today rely on granular site analysis. In water-stressed river basins, evaporative cooling is phased out entirely despite higher electrical draw. Conversely, in regions powered by wind and solar farms, dry air cooling represents a far more sustainable paradigm than water evaporation.

Cooling Technologies and Water Balance

Understanding the thermodynamic mechanisms of cooling topologies is critical to evaluating how equipment selection directly dictates on-site and grid-level water footprints. The industry relies on four dominant architectures:

  • Evaporative Cooling and Open Cooling Towers: Relies on spraying warm water from the secondary loop into an atmospheric airflow. As a fraction evaporates, the remaining fluid cools rapidly before returning to the heat exchanger. In addition to evaporation losses, a portion must be continuously purged (blowdown) to prevent mineral scaling, further increasing water withdrawal. Delivers exceptionally low PUE with minimal compressor power, but introduces microbiological risks (e.g. Legionella), requires chemical treatment, and places intense demand on municipal water supplies.
  • Closed-Loop Systems and Dry Coolers: Thermal waste from server halls is transferred through a closed piping loop to air-cooled dry coolers equipped with high-efficiency fan arrays. The cooling medium (water or water-glycol mixture) circulates in a hermetically sealed circuit without atmospheric contact. There is zero evaporation, fluid loss, or makeup water requirement, achieving complete independence from local water resources. During peak summer heat above $35^\circ\text{C}$, dry coolers lose thermal efficiency and require mechanical chillers, elevating PUE and indirect power-plant water usage.
  • Direct-to-Chip Liquid Cooling (DLC): Coolant (typically deionized water or dielectric glycol fluids) is routed directly through microchannel copper cold plates mounted flush against processor dies (CPUs/GPUs). The external cooling loop can operate in economizer free-cooling mode year-round, eliminating or minimizing direct on-site water consumption. Requires higher upfront capital expenditure, complex quick-disconnect manifolds, and internal rack leak-detection safeguards.
  • Immersion Cooling: Entire server chassis are fully submerged in tanks filled with dielectric fluid (specialized synthetic dielectric hydrocarbons or engineered non-conductive fluids). The fluid directly bathes all components, from silicon dies to motherboards and power supplies. On-site water consumption is virtually zero. Eliminates all server-level fans, achieves class-leading thermal efficiency, and reduces facility footprint, while requiring adapted hardware servicing workflows and higher fluid replacement investments.
Cooling Technology On-Site WUE (L/kWh) Typical PUE Key Advantage Primary Trade-off
Evaporative Towers $1.5 - 3.0+$ $1.10 - 1.15$ Lowest chiller electrical power draw Massive local water evaporation
Dry Coolers $0.0 - 0.2$ $1.25 - 1.40$ Zero on-site water consumption Surge in electrical demand during summer
Direct-to-Chip (DLC) $0.0 - 0.1$ $1.12 - 1.20$ Targeted efficiency for AI accelerators Higher plumbing & manifold complexity
Immersion Cooling $\approx 0.0$ $1.05 - 1.10$ Supports extreme rack power densities Specialized hardware maintenance workflows

Putting the Numbers into Real-World Context

To translate abstract thermodynamic equations into practical understanding, it is essential to ground data center water consumption in context alongside other human and industrial activities. Media headlines frequently spotlight alarming absolute figures; however, comprehensive analysis reveals that claims of "data centers draining the planet dry" are often overstated and detached from broader resource realities.

Absolute Metrics at Facility and User Scale

A modern $100\text{ MW}$ IT capacity data center utilizing conventional or hybrid evaporative cooling consumes an average of $1.0\text{ to }2.0\text{ million liters}$ of direct water daily. This volume corresponds to the typical daily municipal consumption of a modest town of $10{,}000\text{ to }15{,}000\text{ residents}$.

Comparative Benchmarks:

  1. Golf Courses: A standard 18-hole golf course consumes between $1.1\text{ and }1.5\text{ million liters}$ of water daily solely for turf irrigation. In arid climates (such as Arizona, Southern Spain, or the Middle East), a single course routinely consumes upwards of $3.5\text{ million liters}$ per day. One golf course consumes as much or more water than an entire $100\text{ MW}$ hyperscale data center. Globally, over $38{,}000$ golf courses consume billions of liters of fresh water daily for recreational leisure.
  2. Municipal Pipeline Leakage: In numerous European and global urban centers, Non-Revenue Water (NRW) lost to aged, leaking distribution mains accounts for $30\%\text{ to }50\%$ of total treated supply. An average European city of $300{,}000$ residents loses between $20\text{ and }40\text{ million liters}$ of treated drinking water into the ground every day. The infrastructure losses of a single mid-sized municipality surpass the annual water consumption of all data centers in the surrounding region combined.
  3. Agriculture and Livestock: Producing just $1\text{ kg}$ of beef requires an average of approximately $15{,}000\text{ liters}$ of water. A single $150\text{-gram}$ hamburger carries an embedded water footprint exceeding $2{,}200\text{ liters}$. One cup of coffee accounts for $140\text{ liters}$, while manufacturing a single cotton t-shirt demands roughly $2{,}700\text{ liters}$. Forgoing a single beef burger conserves enough water to power over $200{,}000$ generative AI prompts.
WATER FOOTPRINT IN PERSPECTIVE
One burger (150g beef)
~ 2,200 Liters
Cotton T-Shirt
~ 2,700 Liters
Daily irrigation of 1 golf course
~ 1,200,000 Liters
Daily municipal pipeline leakage (1 city)
~ 30,000,000 Liters
100 MW Data Center (daily)
~ 1,500,000 Liters

"Optimizing solely for electrical energy savings often incurs higher on-site water consumption, and vice versa. The true engineering frontier of modern AI infrastructure is not blindly reducing a single metric, but establishing a thermodynamic balance harmonized with local energy and hydrological ecosystems."

Framing data centers as the primary culprits behind local water scarcity frequently serves sensationalist headlines and fuels local opposition (the NIMBY - Not In My Back Yard effect). While enforcing rigorous resource stewardship remains vital, key structural distinctions must be recognized:

  • Data centers operate under stringent financial and ESG governance where water represents a direct operational expense, incentivizing continuous optimization of cooling topologies.
  • An accelerating share of new facilities utilizes reclaimed (grey) water, treated municipal wastewater, or on-site rainwater harvesting instead of municipal potable supplies.
  • With rapid adoption of Direct-to-Chip (DLC) and immersion cooling technologies, on-site water consumption in next-generation facilities is actively trending toward zero.

The question "How much water do data centers actually consume?" does not yield a simplistic two-digit answer. The water footprint of computational infrastructure is a direct function of thermodynamic architecture, geographic siting, and electrical grid decarbonization. While absolute figures of one million liters daily sound formidable, rigorous comparisons against municipal leakage, golf course irrigation, and global agriculture demonstrate that data centers are not the primary catalyst of global water stress. Under regulatory scrutiny and resource economics, the computing industry has emerged as one of the fastest drivers of engineering innovation in water management.

content:
Rušenje biološke dogme

Desetljećima je u razvojnoj biologiji vrijedilo jedno od najnefleksibilnijih pravila: diferencijacija stanica je jednosmjerna ulica. Kada se iz stanica zametka razvije specijalizirana stanica, bilo da je riječ o neuronu koji prenosi električne impulse, stanici kože koja stvara zaštitnu barijeru ili stanici srčanog mišića koja periodički kuca, njezin je put smatran konačnim i ireverzibilnim.

Znanstvenici su taj proces često vizualizirali kao kuglicu koja se kotrlja niz strmu planinu. Jednom kada se kuglica smjesti u najdublju dolinu (određeni tip stanice), njezin povratak na vrh činio se biološki nemogućim. Smatralo se da je stanični identitet trajno zaključan.

Međutim, 2006. godine, ta temeljna biološka dogma doživjela je spektakularan slom.

Japanski znanstvenik Shinya Yamanaka, zajedno sa svojim timom na Sveučilištu u Kyotu, usudio se postaviti pitanje koje je većina smatrala teorijski nemogućim: je li moguće stanični sat vratiti unazad?

Odgovor koji je ponudio protresao je same temelje biomedicine. Yamanaka je dokazao da je proces staničnog sazrijevanja potpuno reverzibilan. Pokazao je da se obična, zrela stanica odraslog čovjeka (poput stanice kože) može reprogramirati i doslovno vratiti na "tvorničke postavke" – u stanje u kojem ponovno ima potencijal postati bilo koji tip tkiva u ljudskom tijelu.

Ovo otkriće, za koje je Yamanaka 2012. godine nagrađen Nobelovom nagradom za fiziologiju ili medicinu, nije bilo samo teorijska pobjeda nad dotadašnjim shvaćanjem biologije. Ono je označilo početak nove ere u kojoj stanični identitet više nije nepromjenjiva sudbina, već stanje koje možemo kontrolirati, obnavljati i usmjeravati.

Što su zapravo OSKM proteini?

Kako bi se uistinu razumjela važnost ovog otkrića, potrebno je zaviriti u mehanizam kojim stanice čuvaju svoj identitet. Svaka stanica u našem tijelu, bilo da je to stanica oka ili stanica jetre, sadrži potpuno isti genetski kod (odnosno istu DNK). Ono što čini stanicu kože različitom od neurona nije sam zapis, već to koji su geni u njoj "uključeni", a koji "isključeni". Taj sustav molekularnih prekidača i oznaka naziva se epigenom.

Tijekom staničnog sazrijevanja, epigenetske oznake čvrsto zaključavaju nepotrebne gene. Yamanaka i njegov tim shvatili su da, žele li stanicu vratiti u prvobitno, nespecijalizirano stanje, moraju pronaći molekularne ključeve koji mogu otključati te epigenetske brave.

Nakon godina testiranja stotina genetskih kombinacija, Yamanaka je došao do zapanjujuće jednostavne formule: bila su dovoljna samo četiri transkripcijska proteina da se zrela stanica vrati u stanje matične stanice. Ti su proteini u znanstvenoj zajednici postali poznati pod zajedničkim nazivom Yamanaka faktori ili akronimom OSKM:

  • Oct3/4 (Octamer-binding transcription factor 3/4): Glavni čuvar pluripotencije. Ovaj protein sprječava stanicu da se diferencira i drži širom otvorena vrata prema svim mogućim staničnim putanjama.
  • Sox2 (SRY-box 2): Djeluje u bliskom partnerstvu s Oct4. Zajedno tvore stabilan kompleks koji kontrolira ekspresiju gena zaduženih za održavanje neograničenog potencijala stanice.
  • Klf4 (Kruppel-like factor 4): Regulira stanični ciklus, potiče preživljavanje stanice tijekom procesa reprogramiranja i pomaže u održavanju stanične samoobnove.
  • c-Myc: Djeluje poput molekularnog "otvarača". c-Myc opušta zbijenu strukturu kromatina (DNK pakiranja), omogućujući ostalim faktorima lak pristup genetskom kodu. Također drastično ubrzava diobu stanica, iako zahtijeva oprez jer je ujedno i poznati onkogen.

Brisanje stanične memorije

Kada se ova četiri proteina unesu u običnu stanicu kože (fibroblast), započinje fascinantan proces:

  1. Proteini se vežu za specifične regije DNK i počinju brisati epigenetsko pamćenje stanice.
  2. Stanica postupno gubi svoju specifičnu funkciju, tj. prestaje se ponašati kao stanica kože.
  3. U roku od nekoliko tjedana, stanica se transformira u induciranu pluripotentnu matičnu stanicu (iPSC).

Pojam pluripotencija označava sposobnost stanice da se razvije u bilo koji od više od 200 tipova stanica u ljudskom tijelu, od kardiomiocita u srcu do fotoreceptora u mrežnici oka. Yamanaka faktori su time dokazali da je stanični identitet zapravo samo softver koji se po potrebi može ponovno formatirati.

Zašto su Yamanaka faktori izazvali revoluciju

Otkriće Yamanaka faktora nije imalo samo teorijski odjek u laboratorijima. Ono je momentalno premostilo neke od najvećih slijepih ulica u koje je moderna medicina upala početkom 21. stoljeća.

Etički preokret: Kraj ovisnosti o embrijima

Prije 2006. godine, jedini poznati izvor pluripotentnih matičnih stanica bili su rani ljudski embriji (blastociste). Istraživanja embrijskih matičnih stanica bila su obavijena žestokim etičkim, pravnim i vjerskim debatama, jer je izdvajanje stanica značilo uništenje embrija. Zbog toga su istraživanja u mnogim zemljama bila strogo ograničena ili potpuno zabranjena. Yamanaka faktori su u potpunosti eliminirali potrebu za korištenjem embrija. Znanstvenici su dobili mogućnost stvoriti neograničene količine pluripotentnih stanica iz običnog uzorka krvi ili male biopsije kože odraslog čovjeka.

Savršeni imunitet: Era autologne (personalizirane) medicine

Jedan od najvećih izazova klasične transplantacijske medicine jest odbacivanje tkiva. Kada pacijentu presadite stanice ili organ druge osobe (alogenična transplantacija), njegov imunološki sustav to prepoznaje kao strano tijelo i napada ga. S induciranim pluripotentnim matičnim stanicama (iPSC), taj problem nestaje. Budući da se stanice uzimaju iz tijela samog pacijenta, reprogramiraju i potom pretvaraju u željeno tkivo, vraćeno tkivo nosi identičan genetski kod i imunološke oznake. Imunološki sustav ga prepoznaje kao vlastito, čime se eliminira rizik od odbacivanja.

Demokratizacija i ubrzanje znanosti

Dobivanje embrijskih stanica zahtijevalo je složena odobrenja i visoke troškove. Yamanaka tehnologija oslanjala se na četiri definirana proteina i standardne laboratorijske protokole, što je omogućilo istraživačima diljem svijeta da započnu vlastita istraživanja matičnih stanica.

Primjena

Sposobnost pretvaranja zrelih stanica u pluripotentne matične stanice preoblikovala je teorijska razmatranja u konkretna medicinska rješenja. Primjena Yamanaka faktora danas se odvija na tri glavna fronta:

Modeliranje bolesti i ispitivanje lijekova in vitro

Prije era iPSC stanica, proučavanje razvoja neurodegenerativnih bolesti u živim ljudskim stanicama bilo je gotovo nemoguće.

  • "Bolest u petrijevoj zdjelici": uzimaju se stanice kože pacijenta koji boluje od specifičnog poremećaja (npr. ALS-a ili Huntingtonove bolesti), reprogramiraju u iPSC stanice, a zatim ih se u laboratoriju usmjerava da se razviju u neurone.
  • Brže i sigurnije testiranje lijekova: Na tim se neuronima mogu testirati tisuće potencijalnih lijekova u stvarnom vremenu bez opasnosti za pacijenta.

Regenerativna medicina i obnova oštećenih tkiva

  • Očne bolesti i sljepoća: U Japanu su pacijentima s teškom makularnom degeneracijom presađeni slojevi stanica mrežnice uzgojeni iz iPSC-a, čime je zaustavljen gubitak vida.
  • Kardiologija: Proizvodnja funkcionalnih kardiomiocita (stanica srčanog mišića) koji se apliciraju na oštećeno područje nakon srčanog udara.
  • 3D organoidi i mini-organi: Uzgoj mikroskopske strukture mozga, bubrega ili jetre u petrijevoj zdjelici radi proučavanja staničnih interakcija.

Parcijalno reprogramiranje: Pomlađivanje i longevity medicina

Ako se OSKM proteini u stanicama aktiviraju na vrlo kratko vrijeme (tzv. prolazno ili pulsno reprogramiranje), stanica ne stigne izgubiti svoj identitet – stanica kože i dalje ostaje stanica kože. Međutim, epigenetski sat stanice se vrati unazad.

  • Resetiranje epigenetske dobi: Parcijalno reprogramiranje čisti epigenetske oznake i molekularni šum nakupljen starenjem.
  • Revolucionarni pokusi: Pokusi na miševima pokazali su da se kratkotrajnom aktivacijom Yamanaka faktora mogu regenerirati oštećeni očni živci, obnoviti mišićna masa starih jedinki i produžiti njihov životni vijek.
  • Budućnost medicine starenja: Biotehnološke investicije (poput Altos Labs) usmjerene su na pretvaranje parcijalnog reprogramiranja u sigurne terapije protiv artritisa, kardiovaskularnih i neurodegenerativnih bolesti.

Izazovi prije šire primjene

Unatoč golemom potencijalu, reprogramiranje stanica nosi znatne biološke izazove:

  • Onkogeni rizik i opasnost od teratoma: c-Myc je poznati onkogen. Ako se stanica reprogramira do stanja potpune pluripotencije unutar žive jedinke bez precizne kontrole, postoji rizik od nastanka teratoma.
  • Izazov dostave do ciljanih tkiva: Potrebno je osigurati dostavu faktora u točno određene organe unutar tijela koristeći sigurnije metode poput sintetske mRNA i lipidnih nanočestica.
  • Tanka linija parcijalnog reprogramiranja: Premalo izlaganja neće učinkovito očistiti nakupljeni epigenetski šum, dok predugo izlaganje uzrokuje da stanica izgubi svoj identitet.
  • Akumulacija izvornih mutacija u DNK: Reprogramiranje resetira epigenetski sat, ali ne popravlja automatski mutacije u samom slijedu nukleotida DNK koje su se nakupile tijekom života.

Pogled u budućnost medicine

Yamanaka faktori promijenili su način na koji gledamo na biologiju starenja i staničnog identiteta. Saznanje da stanična specijalizacija nije jednosmjerna ulica otvorilo je jedno od najuzbudljivijih poglavlja u povijesti medicine. Savladavanje prepreka u dostavi i kontroli reprogramiranja vodi nas prema eri u kojoj medicina neće samo ublažavati simptome kroničnih bolesti, već će moći aktivno regenerirati ljudsko tijelo na staničnoj razini.

Shattering the Biological Dogma

For decades, one of the most inflexible rules in developmental biology held true: cellular differentiation is a one-way street. Once a specialized cell develops from embryonic cells, whether it is a neuron transmitting electrical impulses, a skin cell creating a protective barrier, or a cardiac muscle cell beating rhythmically, its trajectory was considered final and irreversible.

Scientists often visualized this process as a marble rolling down a steep mountain. Once the marble settled into the deepest valley (a specific cell type), its return to the summit seemed biologically impossible. Cellular identity was believed to be permanently locked.

However, in 2006, this fundamental biological dogma suffered a spectacular collapse.

Japanese scientist Shinya Yamanaka, together with his team at Kyoto University, dared to ask a question that most considered theoretically impossible: is it possible to turn back the cellular clock?

The answer he provided shook the very foundations of biomedicine. Yamanaka proved that the process of cellular maturation is completely reversible. He demonstrated that an ordinary mature adult cell (such as a skin cell) can be reprogrammed and literally reset to "factory settings" – into a state where it once again possesses the potential to become any tissue type in the human body.

This discovery, for which Yamanaka was awarded the Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine in 2012, was not merely a theoretical victory over the existing understanding of biology. It marked the beginning of a new era in which cellular identity is no longer an unchangeable fate, but a state that we can control, renew, and direct.

What Are OSKM Proteins Actually?

To truly understand the significance of this discovery, it is necessary to look inside the mechanism by which cells preserve their identity. Every cell in our body, whether it is an eye cell or a liver cell, contains the exact same genetic code (i.e. the same DNA). What makes a skin cell different from a neuron is not the genetic code itself, but which genes are "switched on" and which are "switched off". This system of molecular switches and marks is called the epigenome.

During cellular maturation, epigenetic marks firmly lock away unnecessary genes. Yamanaka and his team realized that if they wanted to revert a cell to its original, unspecialized state, they had to find the molecular keys capable of unlocking these epigenetic padlocks.

After years of testing hundreds of genetic combinations, Yamanaka arrived at an astonishingly simple formula: just four transcription proteins were sufficient to revert a mature cell back to a stem cell state. In the scientific community, these proteins became collectively known as Yamanaka factors or by the acronym OSKM:

  • Oct3/4 (Octamer-binding transcription factor 3/4): The primary guardian of pluripotency. This protein prevents the cell from differentiating and keeps the doors wide open to all possible cellular fates.
  • Sox2 (SRY-box 2): Works in close partnership with Oct4. Together they form a stable complex controlling the expression of genes responsible for maintaining the cell's unlimited potential.
  • Klf4 (Kruppel-like factor 4): Regulates the cell cycle, promotes cell survival during the reprogramming process, and helps maintain cellular self-renewal.
  • c-Myc: Acts like a molecular "opener". c-Myc relaxes the tightly packed chromatin structure (DNA packaging), allowing other factors easy access to the genetic code. It also drastically accelerates cell division, though it requires caution as it is a known oncogene.

Erasing Cellular Memory

When these four proteins are introduced into an ordinary skin cell (fibroblast), a fascinating process begins:

  1. The proteins bind to specific regions of DNA and begin erasing the cell's epigenetic memory.
  2. The cell gradually loses its specific function, i.e., it stops behaving like a skin cell.
  3. Within a few weeks, the cell transforms into an induced pluripotent stem cell (iPSC).

The term pluripotency refers to the ability of a cell to develop into any of the more than 200 cell types in the human body, from cardiomyocytes in the heart to photoreceptors in the retina. Yamanaka factors thus proved that cellular identity is essentially just software that can be reformatted as needed.

Why Yamanaka Factors Triggered a Revolution

The discovery of Yamanaka factors was not merely a theoretical milestone in research laboratories. It immediately bypassed some of the biggest dead ends that modern medicine had encountered in the early 21st century.

Ethical Breakthrough: The End of Embryo Dependency

Before 2006, the only known source of pluripotent stem cells were early human embryos (blastocysts). Research on embryonic stem cells was enveloped in fierce ethical, legal, and religious debates, because harvesting the cells meant destroying the embryo. Consequently, research in many countries was strictly restricted or completely banned. Yamanaka factors completely eliminated the need to use embryos. Scientists gained the ability to generate unlimited quantities of pluripotent cells from an ordinary blood sample or a small skin biopsy from an adult human.

Perfect Immunity: The Era of Autologous (Personalized) Medicine

One of the greatest challenges of classical transplantation medicine is tissue rejection. When you transplant cells or organs from another person into a patient (allogeneic transplantation), their immune system recognizes it as a foreign body and attacks it. With induced pluripotent stem cells (iPSCs), that problem vanishes. Because the cells are taken from the patient's own body, reprogrammed, and then directed into the desired tissue, the returned tissue carries an identical genetic code and immune markers. The immune system recognizes it as self, thereby eliminating the risk of rejection.

Democratization and Acceleration of Science

Obtaining embryonic stem cells required complex regulatory approvals and high costs. Yamanaka technology relied on four defined proteins and standard laboratory protocols, allowing researchers around the world to initiate their own stem cell research.

Applications

The ability to turn mature cells into pluripotent stem cells transformed theoretical considerations into concrete medical solutions. Today, the application of Yamanaka factors unfolds across three main fronts:

Disease Modeling and In Vitro Drug Screening

Before the era of iPSC cells, studying the progression of neurodegenerative diseases in living human cells was nearly impossible.

  • "Disease in a petri dish": Skin cells are harvested from a patient suffering from a specific disorder (e.g. ALS or Huntington's disease), reprogrammed into iPSC cells, and then directed in the lab to differentiate into neurons.
  • Faster and safer drug testing: Thousands of candidate drugs can be tested on these neurons in real time without any danger to the patient.

Regenerative Medicine and Damaged Tissue Repair

  • Ocular diseases and blindness: In Japan, patients with severe macular degeneration received transplants of retinal cell sheets grown from iPSCs, successfully halting vision loss.
  • Cardiology: Generation of functional cardiomyocytes (heart muscle cells) applied to damaged areas following a myocardial infarction.
  • 3D organoids and mini-organ: Growing microscopic structures of the brain, kidney, or liver in a petri dish to study cellular interactions.

Partial Reprogramming: Rejuvenation and Longevity Medicine

If OSKM proteins are activated in cells for a very short duration (so-called transient or pulsed reprogramming), the cell does not have enough time to lose its identity – a skin cell remains a skin cell. However, the cell's epigenetic clock turns backwards.

  • Resetting the epigenetic age: Partial reprogramming clears epigenetic marks and molecular noise accumulated through aging.
  • Groundbreaking experiments: Mouse studies demonstrated that short-term activation of Yamanaka factors can regenerate damaged optic nerves, restore muscle mass in elderly mice, and extend their lifespan.
  • The future of aging medicine: Biotech investments (such as Altos Labs) focus on translating partial reprogramming into safe therapies for arthritis, cardiovascular, and neurodegenerative diseases.

Challenges Before Widespread Clinical Application

Despite immense potential, cellular reprogramming carries significant biological challenges:

  • Oncogenic risk and danger of teratomas: c-Myc is a known oncogene. If a cell is reprogrammed to full pluripotency inside a living organism without precise control, there is a risk of forming teratomas.
  • Delivery challenges to target tissues: Ensuring factors are delivered to specific target organs in the body requires safer vectors like synthetic mRNA and lipid nanoparticles.
  • The fine line of partial reprogramming: Insufficient exposure will not effectively clear accumulated epigenetic noise, while prolonged exposure causes the cell to lose its specialized identity.
  • Accumulation of original DNA mutations: Reprogramming resets the epigenetic clock, but does not automatically repair mutations in the DNA nucleotide sequence accumulated over a lifetime.

Looking Ahead to the Future of Medicine

Yamanaka factors have transformed how we view the biology of aging and cellular identity. Discovering that cellular specialization is not a one-way street opened one of the most exciting chapters in the history of medicine. Overcoming obstacles in delivery and reprogramming control leads us toward an era where medicine will not merely alleviate chronic disease symptoms, but actively regenerate the human body at the cellular level.

title: Peptidi: Biološki signalni molekularni sustavi
summary: Pregled uloge peptida u modernoj medicini – od GLP-1 metaboličke revolucije i regenerativnih spojeva BPC-157 i TB-500 do rejuvenacije, GHK-Cu i primjene umjetne inteligencije u dizajnu de novo peptida.

content:
Većinu je vremena tradicionalna medicina funkcionirala po principu gašenja požara: kada tkivo oboli ili zakaže određeni metabolički proces, medicina reagira sintetskim kemijskim spojevima kako bi blokirala ili pojačala određene funkcije, često uz cijenu sistemskih nuspojava. Međutim, svjedočimo tihoj revoluciji u kojoj se težište s vanjskog "prisiljavanja" organizma pomiče prema davanju preciznih, biološki izvornih uputa samoj stanici. Umjesto da u tijelo unosimo agresivne kemijske strukture, moderna medicina sve češće koristi jezik kojim stanice prirodno komuniciraju – peptide.

Što su zapravo peptidi?

Unatoč tome što u javnosti često zvuče kao novi laboratorijski izum, peptidi su među najstarijim molekulama života. Najjednostavnije rečeno, peptidi su kratki lanci aminokiselina povezani peptidnim vezama. Ako aminokiseline zamislimo kao slova abecede, proteini su opsežne knjige, dok su peptidi kratke, iznimno precizne rečenice. U biokemiji se granica između peptida i proteina obično postavlja na duljini lanca: molekule koje sadrže do $50$ aminokiselina nazivamo peptidima, dok duži lanci tvore proteine.

U ljudskom tijelu peptidi djeluju kao stanični glasnici ili "ključevi" koji se spajaju na točno određene receptore na površini stanica. Kada se peptid veže za svoj receptor, stanici predaje specifičnu poruku: "ubrzaj obnovu tkiva", "potični lučenje hormona", "smanji upalni proces" ili "reguliraj razinu glukoze".

Da bismo razumjeli zašto peptidi zauzimaju središnje mjesto u razvoju suvremenih terapija, korisno ih je usporediti s dva dosadašnja stupa farmakologije:

  • U usporedbi s velikim proteinima (npr. antitijelima): Proteini su velike i kompleksne strukture koje se teško probijaju kroz stanične barijere i tkiva, a imunitet ih nerijetko može prepoznati kao strane objekte i odbaciti. Peptidi su, zahvaljujući znatno manjoj molekularnoj masi, mobilniji, lakše prodiru u ciljana tkiva te znatno rjeđe izazivaju neželjeni imunosni odgovor.
  • U usporedbi s klasičnim sintetskim lijekovima male molekularne mase: Klasični lijekovi često djeluju neselektivno, ciljaju željeni mehanizam, ali usput utječu na niz drugih receptora u tijelu, što rezultira nuspojavama. Peptidi posjeduju visoku afinitetnu specifičnost i djeluju po principu "ključ u bravu". Osim toga, nakon što obave svoju funkciju, tijelo ih razgrađuje na prirodne aminokiseline, čime se drastično smanjuje toksično opterećenje na jetru i bubrege.

Možda i najvažnija spoznaja uvođenjem terapijskih peptida u medicinsku praksu jest da ne mijenjamo fundamentalnu biologiju čovjeka, već joj vraćamo "softverske upute" koje su zbog starenja, bolesti ili ozljeda izostale.

Metabolička revolucija: GLP-1 i nova era u liječenju pretilosti

Desetljećima je tretman pretilosti i metaboličkog sindroma bio zarobljen u pojednostavljenom narativu o "nedostatku volje" i matematici unosa i potrošnje kalorija. Međutim, pojava peptidnih terapija baziranih na crijevno-moždanoj (gut-brain) osi počinje rušiti tu dogmu, ukazujući da je pretilost kompleksna neurobiološka i metabolička bolest regulirana mrežom hormonskih signala.

Agonisti GLP-1 i GIP receptora

Središnji akteri ove revolucije su sintetski analozi prirodnog peptida GLP-1 (Glucagon-like peptide-1), crijevnog hormona koji se prirodno luči nakon obroka i signalizira tijelu prisutnost nutrijenata.

  • Semaglutid (Ozempic, Wegovy): Djeluje tako što imitira prirodni GLP-1: potiče gušteraču na lučenje inzulina kada je razina glukoze povišena, usporava pražnjenje želuca te šalje snažne signale sitosti u hipotalamus.
  • Tirzepatid (Mounjaro, Zepbound): Napravio je dodatni korak kao dvostruki agonist. Osim GLP-1 receptora, aktivira i receptore za GIP. Ova sinergija dvaju peptida ostvaruje još snažniji učinak na osjetljivost na inzulin i razgradnju masnog tkiva.
  • Retatrutid: Najnoviji val istraživanja donosi "triple-G" peptide koji istovremeno stimuliraju GLP-1, GIP i receptore za glukagon. Dodatak glukagonske komponente povećava energetsku potrošnju i potiče izravno sagorijevanje masti u jetri.

Kliničke studije pokazale su da terapija GLP-1 peptidima drastično smanjuje rizik od velikih kardiovaskularnih događaja te značajno poboljšava parametre kod pacijenata s masnom jetrom i kroničnim upalnim procesima. Uvođenjem ovih peptida u medicinsku praksu, pacijenti više ne moraju voditi borbu protiv vlastite biologije.

Regenerativna medicina: Biološko ubrzanje obnove tkiva

Dok se metaboličke terapije bave sistemskim hormonskim signalima, regenerativna medicina fokusirana je na lokalnu obnovu i mikrokruženje oštećenih tkiva. Peptidi u regeneraciji ne potiskuju odgovor tijela, već ubrzavaju i usmjeravaju prirodne reparativne mehanizme.

U središtu istraživanja regenerativnih peptida nalaze se dva spoja koji djeluju komplementarno:

  • BPC-157 (Body Protection Compound-157): Sintetski pentadekapeptid sastavljen od $15$ aminokiselina, deriviran iz želučanog soka. Primarni mehanizam BPC-157 leži u snažnoj promociji angiogeneze (stvaranja novih kapilara). Omogućuje bržu dostavu kisika i nutrijenata u slabije prokrvljena tkiva (tetive, ligamente, hrskavicu) te obnavlja sluznicu probavnog trakta.
  • TB-500 (Sintetski fragment Timozina Beta-4): Djeluje prvenstveno kroz regulaciju aktina, proteina ključnog za građu staničnog kostura. Omogućava stanicama da se lakše kreću prema mjestu ozljede i sprječava prekomjerno stvaranje ožiljkastog tkiva (fibroze).

Sinergija BPC-157 i TB-500 predstavlja izuzetnu strukturu u modernoj ortopediji i sportskoj medicini: BPC-157 gradi krvnu infrastrukturu, dok TB-500 mobilizira stanice graditelje.

Rejuvenacija i anti-aging: Optimizacija staničnog zdravlja

Koncept longevityja (dugovječnosti) i anti-aging medicine koristi peptide za usporavanje samog procesa biološkog starenja.

  • GHK-Cu: Tripeptid povezan s ionom bakra čija razina u krvi drastično opada s godinama (do 60. godine opadne za više od $60\%$). GHK-Cu stimulira proizvodnju kolagena i elastina te modulira ekspresiju više od $4000$ ljudskih gena, vraćajući njihov profil prema mlađem fenotipu.
  • CJC-1295 i Ipamorelin: Sekretagoga peptidi koji potiču hipofizu na lučenje vlastitog hormona rasta ($hGH$). Ova sinergijska primjena oponaša prirodnu fiziološku dinamiku tijela, sprječava sarkopeniju (gubitak mišićne mase) i potiče lipolizu bez gašenja vlastite endokrine funkcije.

Izazovi u primjeni i ograničenja

Najveća prepreka u primjeni peptida jest njihova osjetljivost na probavni sustav, gdje ih proteolitički enzimi brzo razgrađuju. Zbog toga su primarni put primjene supkutane injekcije ili nazalni sprejevi. Ipak, nova biotehnološka rješenja poput SNAC tehnologije omogućuju zaštitu molekule pri oralnoj primjeni.

Kako bi se produžio kratak poluvijek života peptida u tijelu, medicinski kemičari koriste:

  1. Ciklizaciju: Spajanje krajeva lanca u prsten.
  2. Zamjenu aminokiselina: Uvođenje D-aminokiselina.
  3. Spajanje s masnim kiselinama ili PEGilaciju: Produljenje djelovanja (npr. semaglutid ostaje aktivan više od $168$ sati).

Budućnost: AI, de novo sintetski peptidi i ciljana dostava

Evolucija peptidne medicine ulazi u uzbudljivu fazu spajanjem s umjetnom inteligencijom. Sustavi za predviđanje 3D strukture proteina i generativni AI algoritmi omogućuju projektiranje potpuno novih (de novo) peptida od nule, skraćujući razvoj s više godina na svega nekoliko mjeseci.

Također, razvoj konjugata peptid-lijek ($PDC$) omogućuje da peptidi djeluju kao navođeni projektili koji citotoksični teret za uništavanje raka dostavljaju izravno u stanicu tumora, ostavljajući zdravo tkivo netaknutim. Peptidi nas vode u eru precizne medicine gdje liječenje ne znači pritiskanje organizma protiv njegove volje, već obnavljanje njegove prirodne ravnoteže.
content_en:
For most of history, traditional medicine operated on a fire-fighting principle: when tissue gets diseased or a specific metabolic process fails, medicine responds with synthetic chemical compounds to block or enhance certain functions, often at the cost of systemic side effects. However, we are witnessing a quiet revolution in which the focus is shifting from externally "forcing" the organism toward giving precise, biologically native instructions to the cell itself. Instead of introducing aggressive chemical structures into the body, modern medicine increasingly uses the language cells naturally communicate with – peptides.

What Are Peptides, Actually?

Despite often sounding to the public like a new laboratory invention, peptides are among the oldest molecules of life. Simply put, peptides are short chains of amino acids linked by peptide bonds. If we imagine amino acids as letters of the alphabet, proteins are extensive books, while peptides are short, extremely precise sentences. In biochemistry, the boundary between peptides and proteins is usually set at chain length: molecules containing up to $50$ amino acids are called peptides, while longer chains form proteins.

In the human body, peptides act as cellular messengers or "keys" that bind to specific receptors on cell surfaces. When a peptide binds to its receptor, it conveys a specific message to the cell: "accelerate tissue repair", "stimulate hormone secretion", "reduce inflammation", or "regulate glucose levels".

To understand why peptides occupy a central role in the development of modern therapies, it is useful to compare them with the two traditional pillars of pharmacology:

  • Compared to large proteins (e.g. antibodies): Proteins are large and complex structures that have difficulty penetrating cellular barriers and tissues, and the immune system can often recognize them as foreign objects and reject them. Thanks to their significantly lower molecular weight, peptides are more mobile, penetrate target tissues more easily, and far less frequently trigger an undesired immune response.
  • Compared to classic low-molecular-weight synthetic drugs: Classic drugs often act unselectively, targeting the desired mechanism but affecting a number of other receptors in the body along the way, resulting in side effects. Peptides possess high binding affinity specificity and operate on a "lock and key" principle. Furthermore, after completing their function, the body breaks them down into natural amino acids, drastically reducing the toxic burden on the liver and kidneys.

Perhaps the single most important insight from introducing therapeutic peptides into medical practice is that we are not altering fundamental human biology, but rather restoring the "software instructions" that were lost due to aging, disease, or injury.

Metabolic Revolution: GLP-1 and a New Era in Obesity Treatment

For decades, the treatment of obesity and metabolic syndrome was trapped in a simplified narrative of "lack of willpower" and the simple math of calorie intake and expenditure. However, the emergence of peptide therapies based on the gut-brain axis is starting to shatter that dogma, demonstrating that obesity is a complex neurobiological and metabolic disease regulated by a network of hormonal signals.

GLP-1 and GIP Receptor Agonists

The central actors of this revolution are synthetic analogues of the natural peptide GLP-1 (Glucagon-like peptide-1), a gut hormone naturally secreted after meals that signals the presence of nutrients to the body.

  • Semaglutide (Ozempic, Wegovy): Works by mimicking natural GLP-1: it stimulates the pancreas to secrete insulin when glucose levels are elevated, slows gastric emptying, and sends strong satiety signals to the hypothalamus.
  • Tirzepatide (Mounjaro, Zepbound): Took an additional step as a dual agonist. In addition to GLP-1 receptors, it also activates receptors for GIP. This synergy of two peptides achieves an even stronger effect on insulin sensitivity and breakdown of adipose tissue.
  • Retatrutide: The latest wave of research brings "triple-G" peptides that simultaneously stimulate GLP-1, GIP, and glucagon receptors. The addition of the glucagon component increases energy expenditure and promotes direct fat burning in the liver.

Clinical studies have shown that therapy with GLP-1 peptides drastically reduces the risk of major cardiovascular events and significantly improves parameters in patients with fatty liver disease and chronic inflammatory conditions. By introducing these peptides into medical practice, patients no longer have to fight against their own biology.

Regenerative Medicine: Biological Acceleration of Tissue Repair

While metabolic therapies deal with systemic hormonal signals, regenerative medicine focuses on local repair and the microenvironment of damaged tissues. Peptides in regeneration do not suppress the body's response, but accelerate and direct natural reparative mechanisms.

At the heart of regenerative peptide research are two compounds that act complementarily:

  • BPC-157 (Body Protection Compound-157): A synthetic pentadecapeptide composed of $15$ amino acids, derived from gastric juice. The primary mechanism of BPC-157 lies in strong promotion of angiogenesis (formation of new capillaries). It enables faster delivery of oxygen and nutrients to less vascularized tissues (tendons, ligaments, cartilage) and repairs the mucosal lining of the digestive tract.
  • TB-500 (Synthetic Fragment of Thymosin Beta-4): Acts primarily through the regulation of actin, a protein critical for cell cytoskeleton structure. It enables cells to migrate more easily toward the site of injury and prevents excessive formation of scar tissue (fibrosis).

The synergy of BPC-157 and TB-500 represents a remarkable paradigm in modern orthopedics and sports medicine: BPC-157 builds vascular infrastructure, while TB-500 mobilizes builder cells.

Rejuvenation and Anti-Aging: Optimization of Cellular Health

The concept of longevity and anti-aging medicine uses peptides to slow down the process of biological aging itself.

  • GHK-Cu: A tripeptide bound to a copper ion whose level in blood drops drastically with age (by the age of 60, it declines by more than $60\%$). GHK-Cu stimulates collagen and elastin production and modulates the expression of over $4000$ human genes, resetting their profile toward a younger phenotype.
  • CJC-1295 and Ipamorelin: Secretagogue peptides that stimulate the pituitary gland to secrete its own growth hormone ($hGH$). This synergistic application mimics the body's natural physiological dynamics, prevents sarcopenia (loss of muscle mass), and promotes lipolysis without shutting down endogenous endocrine function.

Application Challenges and Limitations

The greatest obstacle in peptide application is their vulnerability to the digestive system, where proteolytic enzymes rapidly degrade them. Because of this, the primary routes of administration are subcutaneous injections or nasal sprays. Nevertheless, novel biotechnological solutions such as SNAC technology enable molecule protection during oral administration.

To extend the short half-life of peptides in the body, medicinal chemists employ:

  1. Cyclization: Joining the ends of the chain into a ring.
  2. Amino Acid Substitution: Introducing D-amino acids.
  3. Fatty Acid Conjugation or PEGylation: Prolonging duration of action (e.g. semaglutide remains active for over $168$ hours).

The Future: AI, De Novo Synthetic Peptides, and Targeted Delivery

The evolution of peptide medicine is entering an exciting phase by combining with artificial intelligence. 3D protein structure prediction systems and generative AI algorithms enable the design of completely novel (de novo) peptides from scratch, shortening development time from several years to just a few months.

Furthermore, the development of peptide-drug conjugates ($PDC$) enables peptides to act as guided missiles that deliver cytotoxic cancer-killing payloads directly into tumor cells, leaving healthy tissue untouched. Peptides are leading us into an era of precision medicine where treatment does not mean coercing the organism against its will, but restoring its natural balance.

title: AlphaFold – prva Nobelova nagrada koju nije dobio čovjek?
title_en: AlphaFold – The First Nobel Prize Not Won by a Human?
summary: Kratki pregled kako je DeepMindov AlphaFold riješio 50 godina star problem savijanja proteina, osvojio Nobelovu nagradu i otvorio novu eru u dizajniranju sintetičkih enzima za pomlađivanje tkiva.
